mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of rising unemployment compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of increasing housing starts compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 1% over two consecutive months signals a contraction in supply, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of declining industrial production compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter, it signals robust consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth over 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher when RSAFS growth exceeds GDPC1 growth compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 over a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of decreasing nonfarm payrolls compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is rising faster than 0.3% per month, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% per month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% per month compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of increasing real GDP compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
